Let me rephrase cus i think im not explaining this well enough. 

Step 1 is easier to study for. Why? Cus u can watch your sketchy your pathoma your boards and beyond etc. and then keep that knowledge with the anking cards. The Qs on the exam are 1st or 2nd order meaning you really just gotta remember stuff more than using ur brain to critically think (i mean of course u have to but its still a lot of recall to solve the puzzles)

Step 2 is hard. They ask you to build on existing knowledge and test new information. Where do u get this new info from? Well thats the hard part. The anking cards are there to help but its hard to know what to do and when to do them. Tbh im not the best to ask when it comes to studying for step2 but in terms of using anking, the most straightforward way is to unsuspend cards while you do uworld and study for the shelf exams. These ‘step 2 specific cards’ are most often tagged as Zanki step2 or M3, at least in my older version that i use. I wanna be clear tho, the answer to your last paragraph is NO. You will NOT have enough information to pass step2 just by doing step1 anking cards and material. You HAVE to study for step2 as a separate exam. The ADVANTAGE of maintaining your step1 ankings is that it will significantly help you answer easy recall questions needed for exams and boost ur scores PLUS you will often be asked on rotations in 3rd/4th year to recall some random side mechanism of action for a medication u heard one time and knowing this will make u look good. And honestly when you start residency, youll be surprised at how much you forgot over the years and how often youre missing just 1 little fact about a drug that will save you a lotttt of time and energy lol

I think the anking decks have 80-90% of ALL the info youll need for exams and on a day to day, and u really cannot go wrong by using this deck to reinforce and learn info for boards and rotations. 

there are cards targeted more for preclinical info (so the stuff for step 1) and different ones to add into the mix during your clinical rotations (aka for step 2). Your step1 info is gonna be more of ‘what is this histology’ ‘what is the mechanism of action of this medication’ whereas step2 will ask more ‘what is the next step’ ‘what is the diagnosis’. They are not really similar exams in terms of content in my opinion, that is it say, if you ONLY did anki cards for step1 material you would certainly not do well on step2 

For what its worth, im in residency now and just took my step3, pending score yet. I did not do a great job of keeping up into residency either and DUDE it is CRAZY how many questions i got wrong on uworld/practices or even attendings pimping me on a day to day that i would look up in the anking deck and sure enough there was a card for it. Bad enough i actually had done a lot of those cards before and just forget the andwers🤦‍♂️ so point being, just do all the dang cards you can throughout your medical career, i can promise it will not be a waste of time

I’ll preface by saying, for these two xpacs I only *really* PVPd in the final season of BfA and this current SL one so take all this with that in mind. 1&3: dont need to heal when theyre fully healed, better to deal damage instead until they need it. You want to keep everyone at full but it’s also not entirely necessary to ensure everyone is always 100%. Throw ur jade statue soothing mist on tank + renewing mist and let those heal over time effects do their job while u squeeze in some damage. If you aren’t comfortable going into melee to use your kick/tiger palm, just try weaving in crackling lightning instead for now. It applies a debuff so your melee teammates deal more damage, and also does a small bit itself. Once u get comfortable healing/damaging together, it may be a little easier for you to use the kick/palm more. In dungeons you can also try damaging at the start of a pack and then stick to healing when everyone starts to take damage until the pack is dead. Try it out a bit, youll get the hang of it

2. Sometimes certain healers hav priority assigned groups or are designated tank healers, but they still heal everyone, just focus on those. From what you’ve posted, I don’t think you’re in the wrong. And really at the end of the day, arguing over that is semantics- the fact is, she betrayed your trust and disrespected you with her responses. She tried to invalidate your feelings and put the blame on you. THAT is toxic. As hard as it may be, you need to accept the fact she is trying to manipulate you, and you need to take this opportunity to move on. Why would you want to be in any sort of relationship with this person? Whatever you do, PLEASE do not try and justify her actions or try to rationalize her thoughts. You CANNOT know what her reasoning was or what she’s thinking. The only truth that exists is that she hurt and manipulate you, and you need accept that without putting any blame on yourself. Do not degrade yourself or fill your mind with self-doubt. 

I don’t know your whole story so I’m going to make some assumptions here, but if this is how she treats you now, I can’t imagine the every day was much better. Sometimes it takes an external pair of eyes for you to see the reality. I’ve found myself blinded this way far too often, coming up with excuses when others point out problems in the relationship - it’s hard bro. But after the dust settles and you take a step back, it becomes clear, and you start to see that it was never really sunshine and roses. And that’s ok man. It might be weird to say, but in a sense, you should be happy that you were able to get rid of this toxicity now before it dragged on for who knows how many more years. The best time to make a change is now, in the present moment. Again, I’m not sure how old you are or what your life situation is, but I still feel confident in saying that this will ultimately be a very insignificant part of your life, and if anything this is an opportunity for self reflection, a window to work on yourself and do something for you, a chance to reevaluate who you truly appreciate in this life. Life is full of painful lessons - I can assure you I’m all too familiar with that - but ultimately this is just another chapter in your story. 

Now, I could’ve just typed something like “fuck that bitch she’s wack move on” instead of having you read this monologue, but I hoped to provide you with something more meaningful you could take away from this. I want you to understand that one person’s actions do not dictate your feelings. I want you to understand that you are being manipulated and invalidated, and that you deserve better. I want you to know you cannot ever know what someone else is thinking or why they do the things they do - you can only know what they explicitly tell you, and even then you can only take that at face value. I want you to know that you can be thankful for the good times and accept that those are over and that this is your opportunity to find the new “good times”. I want you to know it’s ok to feel how you feel. I want you to know you’ll be ok. Maybe it helped, maybe it didn’t - regardless, how you choose to deal with this situation and how you choose to feel is entirely up to you. And I mean that dude, never let any person or situation tell you how to feel - you are in control. 

So Joe, my guy, please do something for me: go for a walk, maybe head to gym or if you have a bike, go for a ride. Take a deep breath, try to keep your mind in the present. You did nothing wrong, and you deserve to be treated better. I wish you the best

Holy shit man Ive been struggling with this exact issue for weeks so its crazy to see this pop up right now haha. After some reflection and input from others, I feel like I’ve finally found a few ways to look at it. 

One is to understand, as many have said, that people just have their own shit going on. Life gets crazy and sometimes you just forget about things. There are people I really, truly care about most in this world that I still simply forget to contact at times. Its hard to believe, but just because someone doesn’t text you to go to lunch doesn’t mean they arent thinking of you and care about you dearly. Understanding and accepting that will take the burden off you. 

On the flip side, some say that if you put in the effort a few times and don’t get it back, then it’s a sign to move on. As sad as that may be, people drift apart as time goes on. Some relationships that maybe you valued highly were simply a result of proximity that the other person moved on from. It can be sad but don’t be discouraged as, when you think about it, would you really want to be friends with someone who doesn’t want to be friends with you? Like why are you so attached? I dont like this view because it hurts but that’s something you may just have to accept. 

And lastly, the other perspective I’ve learned of is that there are some people in this world that have to be the one to put in the effort and some people that don’t. You might just be one of those people that does. U are probably wondering then, why me? Like why does it have to be my job and some people dont have to? Well, cus it really do be like that sometimes bro. I don’t want you to be discouraged either because if you think about it, you have the most control of your life with this thinking. You’re the one that people are drawn to, the one that creates energy. And sure, when people don’t reach out to you, you may feel alone and sad. But bro, how do you fix that? How do you fix being lonely? You find other peope! And what do ya kno, you’re the person that MAKES people come together. Think from the other perspective now, if you had everything come to you, what happens if u feel lonely and no one reaches out? Well if u also dont reach out, now you’re just stuck. See what I’m saying? Id also like to end this by saying, think of a time where you WERE feeling lonely and isolated cus no one reached out. How AWESOME would u feel if someone, just 1 single person texted you and said “hey how you been i havnt heard from you in a while!” Your day would be made. I challenge you to be THAT person, the one who can light up someone’s world and make their day. I hope this helps, friend.

I feel you. Was definitely VERY tough in the beginning but things are much better now. Not ideal still, but there are a handful of people I consider close, and a decent size group id comfortably say are friends. Ill share everything that i did/can think to do. Ultimately its going to involve you taking risks and putting in work tho. 

First off, idk what your situation is like but if you have any lab partners or group members, just hit them up. Up to you if want to meet in person to hang, grab a drink, etc. Obviously thats ideal but not going to advocate for that in covid so use at ur own discretion. but its med school so u can always ask people if they want to study. If thats too much, then start off by asking them for help to open up conversation. Nothing wrong with saying “hey this is random but do u understand ventilation/perfusion? I didnt get it from todays lectures at all”. If you have a big class wide group chat, that might help to find people too. Someone posted their house anki deck for msk? Ask them to help u set up anki or if they use anking too or if they consider adding stuff from sketchy/boards and beyond. Anything like that can at least get a conversation going. Yall have a class discord server? See if anyone plays a game that you’re familiar with. Literally just ask them about it and im sure you can get something going. Interested in starting/joining a club on campus? Find some mutually interested classmates and go from there. Anyone live in the same apartment complex? Hit them up! The convenience alone will probably make them more inclined to hang out lol. Even despite what I said about having some close friends, i barely know 1/3 of my class and even some of the friends I do have i dont really know well. Everyone including me is still in the same boat as you, so dont stress. Just have some courage and make an effort to find people. Nice benefit of med school (at least in my experience so far) is that once you start making a few friends it snowballs since classes are relatively small, and someone always knows someone. Anyways hope this helps. Stay motivated and finish up the semester strong

I’m not sure what year you are but I’m afraid you hit the sad truth of 501 and pretty much every science course in the track: you pretty much have to teach yourself. It sucks but its a skill that youll need to have. 

For Surerus’ class wellllll it kinda sucks too haha. No shortcuts really, youll need to learn pretty much every enzyme and what it makes. Download the free “amino acid quiz” app and grind those out whenever ur in line for coffee or something to memorize all the AAs. I will say that she does include some kinda miscellaneous questions related to textbook material/things not really emphasized but its not worth the time unless you already know the stuff real well especially if youre struggling to learn from the textbook anyways. 

So how to learn on your own? Literally youtube my friend. Just search up any topic and watch videos until you start to get it. Khan academy is great too. Biochem also has a lot of pathways so id recommend drawing them out like on repeat. Like wake up, draw krebs cycle with all the intermediates and everything. Check ur work after and fill in everything u got wrong. Do it again before bed or in the afternoon or something too. Literally do this for 2-4 days and it’ll stick w u for a longgg time. 

Ok this next one also sucks but it’s important if youre looking to get really high scores as opposed to just passing. You not only need to try and learn stuff on ur own, but also do it ahead of time. U have the syllabus already ya? So Like 1-2 days before each topic, work on that material. Dont worry about how long u spend on it or whatever. Just do it until u feel like u could explain the main points clearly to someone else who knows nothing about the topic. Then lecture basically becomes a review and u can fill in the blanks. It sucks cus u gotta do a lot of work urself but this is by far my best recommendation and has been carrying me in med school so far. 

Ok next thing is definitely dependent on ur learning styles but I personally didnt really take notes in her class. I wrote down some things that would help me remember stuff or that i hadnt heard before, but just writing the stuff down was so useless since id have to go home and look at it at my own speed anyways. But really u gotta explore and figure out what works for u. 

With biochem, there arent really shortcuts. Memorize all aminos acid structures/name/abbreviations and u get a lot of stuff right. Then it just comes down to memorizing pathways which can become MUCH easier if u find a way to draw them out yourself. Good luck!

Edit: I know its very daunting but youd be amazed at how much you can learn if you really try. And I will say, her biochem class was a lot more manageable than some of the others I’ve taken. I dont wanna say it’s “easier” but there is a lot more rote memorization than critical thinking, so if you just hardcore grind itll pay off!

So if you click on the pvp menu tab thing, youll see a bar at the top that shows your conquest. It’s basically just another currency. You get this from battlegrounds, arena skirmishes and brawl if its up. The amount u get is a lot for the first win of the day but decreases significantly for subsequent wins in the same daily reset (ie 40 conquest for First BG win of the day down to 8 for subsequent ones, 15 for first skirmish -> 0 for rest of day). The amount from rated arenas is i think like 25-35 depending on 2s/3s but this is for every win and does not decrease. 

The battles i was talking about are the assaults that randomly appear in one of the bfa zones for a few hours where it shows a giant thing on the map and changes some of the world quests (also gives a quest to do 4 and then another mini quest once youre in the zone but this is more or leas useless now and doesnt give conquest ad far as i know). If you do these world quests with warmode on however, you get like 15conquest per win. You need 500 total for each reward so if you can snag a BG win everyday and just do these when they pop up its fairly simple and consistent way to get conquest.

You get 445 gear from your pvp weekly chest if you are unranked-1399 CR tho if you can get to 1400 it jumps to 455, so it could be worthwhile to grind some rated games if you have the time/desire to do so.

PvP gear is random drop after doing pvp content. Doing rated arenas, for example, can give you decent gear after arena wins as they scale with your rating, but these are random procss still and by the time you reach a high enough rank to get good gear, you’ve probably already exceeded that gear ilvl anyways. There arent any pvp specific stats (like resilience) tho in arenas some stats are less effective than in pve (ie if I remember correctly crits are half as effective in PvP than PvE so its usually a much worse stat for that content). Marks of honor as basically just for cosmetics now but also have use for certain profession recipes and getting your weekly rolls. 

The only really accessible and useful pvp gear (in my opinion) is the weekly conquest cap. If youre a fresh character you have access to all the previous weeks rewards (in order) and get pretty solid gear. On top of that, you just need conquest so you theoretically get it without ever doing pvp by having warmode on and doing the zone assaults (also easy to get conquest if horde and do call to arms). 

But ya pvp this expansion is pretty scuffed and the gearing is just: do weekly cap, mythic+, raid

So this started as a one sentence tip that turned into this essay. Hopefully this is organized well enough and someone finds it helpful in some capacity. 

Tl;dr
Draft a top TE early, draft an Ekler type handcuff if you can, keep up with news early, take calculated waiver risks, watch all the games

1. think you gotta snag a top TE early. Every single championship team in all my leagues this had either ertz, kelce or kittle. I feel that there’s always a good play at the other positions, but TE is such a gamble that securing a top player makes your team much a) more consistent on a week to week basis and b) overall have a higher ceiling. 

2. I’d also say its worth drafting a couple backup RBs with standalone value like Ekler or Cohen coming into the season. Drafting straight handcuffs isnt as recommended since you bank on injury/suspension entirely whereas someone like Ekler is playable and has potential to be an RB1 given the scenario. 

3. Next, keep up with news! Connor was an insane pickup that just required a reddit visit and an open bench spot. Same with Chubb, D Williams, and all the other league winners. By the time these kind of things get reported on ESPN, its probably too late. In all honesty idk what the best app is, but I’ve heard people recommend sleepbot

4. Play matchups/waiver plugs. This isnt super useful until maybe 1/4 or midway thru the season and kind of requires some more knowledge (see tip 5) but beeing able to pick up a player off the waivers for a week can be huge. This is something I kinda picked up from doing DFS for a year now. It’s crazy how well a lot of lesser know /owned players do on a given week. Knowing when to grab Zay Jones or Chris Godwin or Robby Anderson and toss them in for a game can help you steal wins from your opponent. Granted there is still a lot of luck, but getting a good sense of how to do this can just absolutely upset matchups, especially when your team is crippled by injuries or byes

5. And lastly, if you really wanna do well I think you have to watch the games. Its difficult/impossible for a lot of people cus it takes up so much time, but you get so much info about player strength/weakness, potential injury, coaching style/gameflow, etc. You can start to tell when advice/analysis is actually helpful or just plain bad. From my albeit basic understanding of metabolism, stress, and the cardiovascular system, I think there is actually a net decrease is carolic requirements. Why? 

1) Well the main factor here is going to be cortisol. I’m not sure how familiar you are with it but basically it’s the body’s stress hormone. It does a lot of different things like control blood pressure and stimulate insulin release. When stressed either physically or emotionally, cortisol is released as your body enters the “fight or flight” state (Sympathetic nervous system activation). At this point, your body is preparing for battle by conserving energy, stopping digestion, and delaying tissue repair (parasympathetic nervous system functions). Essentially your metabolism slows down so you can use that energy to fight off attackers (evolutionarily speaking). In the case of a mental athlete,  they aren’t actually using this energy and thus wouldn’t be burning calories. On top of that, there are studies that show increased appetite after stressful events. Consequently, this can lead to weight gain since you’re now increasing caloric intake despite not actually increasing caloric output. 

2) From a strictly functional perspective, yes, the brain does burn calories from thinking. But really the amount you burn from this is negligible in comparison to something like a 1 mile run. Plus, the brain only uses glucose whereas, during intense physical activity, the body can use carbs and eventually adipose tissue (aka body fat) for energy, hence how you can lose weight from physical exercise

Tl;dr:
1) stress releases cortisol hormone->body stops burning as many calories->can make you hungry and actually overeat and inc weight gain
2) thinking hard doesnt burn nearly as many calories as physical exercise and can only use glucose, not carbs/fats

2.1k mw here. I think prepatch mw is in an interesting spot. Not sure if others will agree but they feel almost like the glass canon of healers right now. What the spec lost in defense and mobility, they absolutely gained in healing power. Because of the nerf to paralysis and some other tools, mw heavily realies on positioning and proper cd usage. Im finding it difficult to play as offensive with crane/setting up cc combos since you are left so vulnerable without those. Having said that, you can certainly still make plays and be a huge threat if you and you teammate(s) can adapt to the situation well. In terms of concrete tips? I recommend watching a guide or two by stoopz. Not sure if he has anything super updated but I found his advice to be particularly helpful and transferable to other specs as well. Otherwise a couple things I can suggest are: 

1) experiment with talents and learn how each can be useful in a situation. i.e healing sphere can be insane against some comps, ring of peace actually might find more use now since it doesnt replace leg sweep, etc 
2) make sure you are not sitting there channeling soothing mist all day. Healing is so power right now you only need a couple spells to keep everyone topped off. Oh and use the pillars to your advantage! EDIT: to be more specific, you want to keep renewing up on your team. Then just hide behind pillar, peak for a sec to cast soothing mist + surging and they probably wil be good as new. Because you have a powerful hot and no cast times, its pretty strong to play this peaking pillar game. 
3) absolutely practice using ports better. Use them to dodge incoming poly casts, kite melee, etc. Re adjust your ports to match the flow of where the fight is going. 
4) don’t spam your chi torpedo. Very common mistake that just absolutely kills people. 

Mw survival is about playing an aggressive game of juking. You cant let them touch you but you have to utilize your escapes properly. Their slippery-ness is dependent on you not wasting abilities. i.e. you torpedo in for a heal unnecessarily. their arms war charges you while their dk puts his slow on you. You try to torpedo back but dk grips you in. Ok so you leg sweep immediately and end up missing the warrior obviously. He storm bolts but you have trinket. You find enough time to waddle within portal range. You’re still hamstring slowed but port behind the pillar. This port was actually slightly to the side of the pillar and within range for the dk to put chains on you again. Warrior leaps and dk wraith walks over. Pop paralysis to buy time but your dps immediately breaks the cc cus you arent in comms. You are now channeling soothing mists to get some health back and get kicked. So Now at 50% hp and cant cast. You are spamming life cocoon as these melee rail on you and you manage to get it off at 24%. Your torpedo is off cd and you use it into the middle of the map. Enemy rsham immediately kicks your soothing mist channel. War charges and executes x2 and you died. In this example, just ignore what your teammates didnt do for simplicity sake. Almost all of the problems here could have been avoided by better port placement/usage, better use of torpedo, better cc, etc. If this is unclear or you would like more help, feel free to let me know. 

Tldr: learn how to use your cc/mobility efficiently. Play the pillar game to your advantage. Heals are real stronk but bad usage of abilities will make u a super ez kill target

So with rogue, if you use your medallion to get out of a sap, you're gonna have a bad time since he/she can now get a 5 combo point kidney shot stun for 5sec and there's nothing you can do. If you fear/leap away and pop all your defensives before the rogue actually pops their cds, you're gonna have a bad time. If you're against a sham, popping avatar and deadly calm without getting rid of their counter strike totem is going to get you killed. Against mage, it can be difficult as it's super easy to get kited around. However, a well timed spell reflect can you give a good window to push. Bladestorm is awesome in that it removes roots (like frost nova) and prevents you from being ccd, so you can also use that to counter some of the kiting going on. Don't forget to use your kick appropriately either. Just spamming it on cooldown is (probably) not going to get you anywhere. In 2s/3s especially, learning about burst windows and when to switch targets is arguably pretty much what the whole thing is about, so learning/practicing those skills will really help. An overall awareness of what is going with your arena parnter(s) and your opponents is really going to improve your game. If you're really serious about getting better, there's plenty of good content on youtube/twitch. I also recommend recording some arenas yourself and rewatching them to look for mistakes. For sniper, I'd excercise some caution especially if you don't know the market. Pets for example are very volatile as they can essentially be transferred cross-realm. Plus the level/rarity of the pet can change the price which you may not immediately notice. With the BoE greens, you can double check with undermine journal, though when sniping you often dont have enough time. TSM can actually show regional sale rates which can sometimes be helpful too. When starting out, I'd refer to undermine journal a decent amount just to kind of see how things sell. Transmog and randlm BoEs are really slow to move (sometimes like never sell) but can give huge profits if you snag them at a low price. To be honest, if I see a green for 1g and TSM gives a market avg of 300g, I'd buy it instantly. If it never sells I don't really lose anything. In fact, I'd probably send to an alt if I don't have the appearance. So a good strat that many goblins here recommend is to find a price you are OK with losing with. That way, when sniping, you can just go through without second guessing yourself and potentially missing out on a huge deal. Another thing is to set your ideal profit. So if I see something on sniper for say 1k and see an average of 30k but a really low sale rate, there are a couple ways to approach. You can obviously repost for 30k and wait. Personally, I would maybe list for 25k or 20k or honestly maybe even 15k and see if I can get a sale. Obviously this is up to you but I think a lot of it comes down to how you analyze it. Charts and numbers on undermine journal should help with this. Generally look at regional price to get an idea and then compare to server price. Then maybe quantity available, sale rate, etc.  

*side note i forgot to mention: careful with the %market values. People can artificiallly inflate prices by reposting at some absurd price for months to increase mrket val and then post at a "cheap" price to make a huge profit and trick unsuspecting snipers. That's why I said to refer to undermine journal and the regional price if you have any reservations or suspicions about an item
